name: David Banner
notes: A rapper-producer, so this model is his production workflow: crunk 808 aggression with piano and string writing on top of it. The research calls the sustained 4-bar chord loop under a 2-bar riff *unusual for crunk — most of the lane has no chords at all*, and that is exactly what separates this file from its siblings. It is the only entry in this batch with four-chord families and real voice-leading (`topVoiceStepwise` true, `extensions.seventh` 0.24, an open voicing), and the only one whose melody block is written as a keyboard part rather than a stab — `densityPerBar` [3, 8], an arch/descend contour instead of a flat riff, and `structure` left as the loop because the riff is still 2 bars. Both progressions the research names are authored: i–VI–III–VII and i–iv–i–V. ⚠ `confidence` is medium and **the harmonic detail is the inferred parameter** — the research sources the self-production credit and the chart facts, and says the harmony is inference from his documented piano-forward approach. `session.bpm` is additionally marked [LOW-CONF]. ⚠ Two bands are documented: 70–82 half-time for the club cuts and 80–90 straight for the soul/piano material. This model takes the club band, because that is the one his crunk placements sit in; the ballad side is not reachable from it, and neither is the "frequent half-time/normal-time section contrast within one track" the research describes, which has no parameter. ⚠ The doubled low piano octave under the 808 is a layering the engine has no stage for; `bass808.slideProb` 0.16 carries only the pitch-drop at phrase ends. ⚠ Fill fingerprint for this batch: `gapProb` 0.28 / `descendProb` 0.54 / `rampJitter` 21. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts.
